reader_blockers: Passage §2 contains a self-contradictory claim: 'The undisturbed oysters laid down more nacre, and laid it faster, and they did so right across the bay — in the leases that fussed endlessly over their panels and in the leases that barely touched them, alike.' The design assigns disturbance at lease level ('varying just one thing: whether a lease turned and cleaned its panels on a frequent cycle ... or left them very largely alone'), so 'undisturbed oysters' cannot exist 'in the leases that fussed endlessly over their panels'. The subgroup-invariance clause is logically impossible as written.

Q2 option A reproduces that impossible clause almost verbatim, so the only text-supported answer to Q2 is the one a careful reader would reject as incoherent. On a second read I stalled here and had to answer A by elimination rather than by comprehension; that is unfair to a student who reads closely.
reader_notes: Everything else in the unit is unusually well written and the argumentative arc (thickness vs. roundness, threshold, narrow window) is clear and consistent.
Q5 option B is long and clause-heavy compared with A/C/D; length is a mild give-away for the qualified-attitude answer.
The two glossary lines (nacre, mantle) are well chosen and genuinely needed for §3.
